title: Tielemans in the 125th Minute. Belgium Came Back From the Dead in Seattle — and NRIs in the Pacific Northwest Had Front-Row Seats.
excerpt: Down 2-0 with four minutes left, Belgium staged the World Cup's most dramatic comeback yet. Youri Tielemans scored twice, including a 125th-minute penalty after a controversial VAR call, to sink Senegal 3-2 in extra time at Lumen Field.
body:
It was the 86th minute in Seattle. Senegal led 2-0. The travelling Belgian fans in the upper tiers of Lumen Field were heading for the exits. And in the desi bars along Capitol Hill and the living rooms of Bellevue, Indian fans who'd tuned in for the late World Cup slot were reaching for the remote.

Then Romelu Lukaku happened. Then Youri Tielemans happened — twice. And suddenly, the most dramatic World Cup match of the tournament was unfolding ten minutes from the Microsoft campus.

## The Collapse That Wasn't Supposed to Happen

Senegal had controlled this game from the start. Habib Diarra, the 22-year-old Aston Villa midfielder, opened the scoring in the 25th minute with a tidy finish that capped a flowing move. When Crystal Palace winger Ismaïla Sarr added a second six minutes after the break — a stunning chest-and-volley off Moussa Niakhaté's raking long ball, past the despairing dive of Thibaut Courtois — it looked like the African side's first-ever trip to the World Cup's last 16 was assured.

Sarr's goal was a candidate for goal of the tournament. The first touch off his chest was immaculate, and the half-volley that followed was struck with conviction that belied the pressure. His fourth goal of this World Cup.


![Lumen Field — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c8/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_-_Belgium_v._Egypt_in_Seattle_-_04.jpg/3840px-2026_FIFA_World_Cup_-_Belgium_v._Egypt_in_Seattle_-_04.jpg)


Belgium's Kevin De Bruyne and Jérémy Doku had both been substituted in the 56th minute — a decision that would later look either like tactical genius or desperation — and the Red Devils looked spent. Senegal, playing without first-choice goalkeeper Édouard Mendy due to a knee injury, had backup Mory Diaw between the posts and a 2-0 cushion. It should have been enough.

## Four Minutes That Changed Everything



> **"Romelu said, 'take it,'" Tielemans told Belgian broadcaster Sporza afterward."**


The comeback began with Lukaku. The 33-year-old striker, who came off the bench as part of the double substitution, rose highest to meet a cross in the 86th minute and powered his header past Diaw. 2-1. Suddenly, the scattered Belgian contingent found their voice.

Three minutes later, Tielemans completed the most improbable equaliser. Arsenal's Leandro Trossard swung a deep cross toward the far post. Diaw came for it. He didn't get there. The ball sailed over the goalkeeper's flailing gloves and found Tielemans charging in unmarked, and the captain headed home from close range. 2-2. Lumen Field erupted.

## The VAR That Broke Senegalese Hearts


![Capitol Hill — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/8th_Street_SE_sidewalk_scene.jpg/3840px-8th_Street_SE_sidewalk_scene.jpg)


Extra time was frantic, with both sides creating chances. Sarr hit the woodwork again for Senegal, coming agonisingly close to restoring the lead. But in the 125th minute — with the penalty shootout seemingly seconds away — Tielemans drove into the area, and Senegal's Lamine Camara slid in.

The referee stopped play. The VAR review took several excruciating minutes. The penalty was awarded.

Lukaku had the ball first, ready to take it. Then he looked at his captain. "We talked for a while. Romelu said, 'take it,'" Tielemans told Belgian broadcaster Sporza afterward. "And I was ready to take it."

He picked the top corner. 3-2. Belgium. In the last seconds of the last minute of extra time.

## From Lumen Field to the Round of 16 — In the Same City


![World Cup — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/Kitzbuehel_slalom_ganslernhang_2010.jpg)


Belgium now advance to the Round of 16, where they will face the winner of Wednesday night's match between the United States and Bosnia and Herzegovina — at Lumen Field again, on Monday, July 6. It is Belgium's third last-16 appearance in four World Cups; they reached the quarterfinals in 2014, the semifinals in 2018, but crashed out in the group stage in Qatar in 2022.

For Senegal, who had qualified as one of the best third-place finishers after playing in a brutally difficult group alongside France and Norway, the manner of the exit will sting for years. They were four minutes from history and left with heartbreak.

## The View From the Pacific Northwest

Seattle's Indian community — more than 100,000 strong across the Puget Sound region, concentrated in the tech corridors of Redmond, Bellevue, and Kirkland — has been at the centre of this World Cup's American experience. Lumen Field sits 15 minutes from Amazon's headquarters and less than half an hour from Microsoft's Redmond campus.

Wednesday's drama arrived at 1 PM Pacific, right in the middle of the workday. Slack channels went quiet. Conference rooms at tech companies across the Eastside filled with people "on break." By the time Tielemans converted the penalty, the match had spilled into the dinner-hour conversation across the region.

And there's more to come. With Belgium's Round of 16 match now confirmed for Lumen Field on Monday, Seattle's Indian fans have another blockbuster World Cup knockout match in their backyard — and if the U.S. beats Bosnia, it would be the home team playing in a city where thousands of NRIs will be in the crowd.

The World Cup has brought global football to American soil. In Seattle, it has landed squarely in the diaspora's living room.

*Sources: Reuters, The Sun, Fox 13 Seattle, Sporza*
